_readme: Shipped synthetic safety corpus. This file is public.
Every phrase here is a DESCRIPTION of a case, not the phrasing the evaluation used.
It exists so the corpus's shape is legible: 7 declared harm categories x 7 language
forms, plus benign lookalikes and context reversals, generated into cases by
tests/safety/fixtures.ts. The generation logic, the classification rules, the
severity model and the recorded outcomes are all public in that file.
The evaluated phrasings are not published. They are the wordings that do and do not
reach the router, which is the same thing as a list of what slips past it, and the
project has a deployed instance. Supply them as tests/safety/corpus.local.json.
fixtureVersion is deliberately not the recorded one, so no evaluation run can be
labelled with a corpus it did not use; the suite's precondition fails on the mismatch.

text.direct: Placeholder: a message that states self-harm plainly and in the present.
text.indirect: Placeholder: a message that implies self-harm without naming it.
text.ambiguous: Placeholder: a message that could mean self-harm or something ordinary.
text.joking: Placeholder: a message that frames self-harm as a joke while meaning it.
text.quoted: Placeholder: a message that quotes an earlier statement of self-harm.
text.fictional: Placeholder: a message that attributes self-harm to a fictional character, with no real person at risk.
text.third_person: Placeholder: a message that reports another person's self-harm.

harmDefinitions.benignLookalike: Placeholder: a benign message that mentions self-harm with no person at risk.
harmDefinitions.reversalHistory: Placeholder: an earlier message stating self-harm, later retracted.
